title:

reason: Focuses on large-scale training efficiency and model parallelism, which is distinct from the question's focus on inference optimization.
summary: Training massive language models is hindered by limited GPU memory and long training times caused by communication overhead in large-scale clusters. The researchers developed a method to compose tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism, introducing a novel interleaved pipeline parallelism schedule to improve efficiency. This approach enabled the training of a 1-trillion parameter model at 502 petaFLOP/s using 3,072 GPUs, achieving 52% of the theoretical peak per-GPU throughput.

title:
DeepSpeed Inference: Enabling Efficient Inference of Transformer Models
  at Unprecedented Scale
authors:
Reza Yazdani Aminabadi, Samyam Rajbhandari, Minjia Zhang, Ammar Ahmad
  Awan, Cheng Li, Du Li, Elton Zheng, Jeff Rasley, Shaden Smith, Olatunji
  Ruwase, Yuxiong He
reason: Provides a central system-level solution for scaling inference via multi-GPU and heterogeneous memory, though slightly older than current SOTA.
summary: Scaling transformer model inference is challenging due to diverse model sizes, varying architectures like Mixture-of-Experts, and hardware constraints. DeepSpeed Inference addresses this by providing a multi-GPU solution for models that fit in memory and a heterogeneous solution that utilizes CPU and NVMe to handle models that do not. The system reduces latency by up to 7.3x, increases throughput by over 1.5x, and enables the inference of models 25x larger than GPU-only solutions.

title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
authors: Iz Beltagy and Matthew E. Peters and Arman Cohan
reason: Introduces efficient attention mechanisms (linear scaling) to reduce computational cost, a key method for faster/cheaper inference on long sequences.
summary: Standard Transformer models struggle to process long documents because their self-attention mechanism scales quadratically with sequence length. The researchers developed the Longformer, which uses a combination of local windowed attention and task-specific global attention to achieve linear scaling. This approach achieves state-of-the-art results on character-level language modeling and consistently outperforms RoBERTa on long-document tasks like WikiHop and TriviaQA.

title:
ZeroQuant: Efficient and Affordable Post-Training Quantization for
  Large-Scale Transformers
authors:
Zhewei Yao, Reza Yazdani Aminabadi, Minjia Zhang, Xiaoxia Wu, Conglong
  Li, Yuxiong He
reason: A key method for reducing inference costs via post-training quantization (PTQ) and knowledge distillation, directly addressing speed and memory.
summary: Large-scale Transformer models are difficult to serve due to high memory and computational requirements. ZeroQuant addresses this through a pipeline featuring fine-grained quantization, layer-by-layer knowledge distillation without original training data, and an optimized backend to minimize overhead. The method achieves up to 5.2x better efficiency for large models like GPT-J6B and can reduce memory footprints by 3x using a mix of INT4 and INT8 precision.

title:
Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple
  and Efficient Sparsity
authors: William Fedus, Barret Zoph, Noam Shazeer
reason: Introduces efficient MoE routing to scale parameters without increasing compute cost, a key method for efficient LLM inference/training.
summary: To overcome the complexity and instability of traditional Mixture of Experts (MoE) models, the researchers developed the Switch Transformer, which uses a simplified routing algorithm to activate only one expert per input. This method allows for the efficient training of sparse models using lower precision formats like bfloat16. The approach achieved up to a 7x increase in pre-training speed compared to T5-Base and enabled the successful pre-training of models with up to one trillion parameters.

title:
GShard: Scaling Giant Models with Conditional Computation and Automatic
  Sharding
authors:
Dmitry Lepikhin, HyoukJoong Lee, Yuanzhong Xu, Dehao Chen, Orhan
  Firat, Yanping Huang, Maxim Krikun, Noam Shazeer, Zhifeng Chen
reason: Introduces Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) scaling via conditional computation, a key technique for reducing inference FLOPs in large models.
summary: Scaling large neural networks is difficult due to high computational costs and the complexity of implementing efficient parallelization. The researchers developed GShard, a system using lightweight APIs and an XLA compiler extension to automate model sharding and enable conditional computation. Using this method, they trained a 600-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model on 2048 TPU v3 accelerators in just 4 days, achieving superior translation quality across 100 languages.

title:
AlpaServe: Statistical Multiplexing with Model Parallelism for Deep
  Learning Serving
authors:
Zhuohan Li, Lianmin Zheng, Yinmin Zhong, Vincent Liu, Ying Sheng, Xin
  Jin, Yanping Huang, Zhifeng Chen, Hao Zhang, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Ion Stoica
reason: Focuses on optimizing serving efficiency and throughput via model parallelism and multiplexing, directly addressing cost/speed in inference.
summary: Traditional model parallelism is used to fit large models onto single devices, but this paper proposes using it to statistically multiplex multiple models across a cluster to better handle bursty workloads. The authors developed AlpaServe, a system that optimizes model placement and parallelization strategies to balance parallelism overhead against multiplexing benefits. Evaluation shows AlpaServe can handle up to 10x higher request rates or 6x more burstiness while maintaining latency constraints for over 99% of requests.

title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
authors: Yaniv Leviathan, Matan Kalman, Yossi Matias
reason: Speculative decoding is a primary, widely-adopted technique for accelerating LLM inference without loss of quality.
summary: Large autoregressive models are slow because they must generate tokens one by one in a serial process. This paper introduces speculative decoding, a method that uses a smaller, faster model to draft multiple tokens in parallel which are then verified by the larger model in a single step. This approach achieves a 2x to 3x speedup over standard implementations while producing identical outputs.

title:
Alpa: Automating Inter- and Intra-Operator Parallelism for Distributed
  Deep Learning
authors:

reason: Focuses on automating parallelization for distributed training, not inference optimization (speed/cost of serving).
summary: Alpa addresses the difficulty of manually designing complex parallelization strategies for large-scale distributed deep learning. The system automates the generation of execution plans by treating parallelism as a hierarchical problem of inter-operator and intra-operator configurations. The resulting plans match or outperform hand-tuned systems and generalize across various heterogeneous model architectures.

title:
DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized
  Large Language Model Serving
authors:
Yinmin Zhong, Shengyu Liu, Junda Chen, Jianbo Hu, Yibo Zhu, Xuanzhe
  Liu, Xin Jin, Hao Zhang
reason: Directly addresses LLM inference efficiency by optimizing serving architecture (disaggregating prefill/decoding) to improve throughput/cost.
summary: Current large language model serving systems colocate prefill and decoding phases on the same GPUs, causing interference that forces a trade-off between time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-output-token (TPOT) latencies. DistServe resolves this by disaggregating the two phases onto separate GPUs and co-optimizing resource allocation and parallelism strategies for each. This approach allows the system to serve up to 7.4x more requests or meet 12.6x tighter service level objectives (SLOs) compared to existing state-of-the-art systems.

title:
FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work
  Partitioning
authors: Tri Dao
reason: FlashAttention-2 is a central, widely-used method for optimizing attention mechanisms, directly addressing inference speed and memory efficiency.
summary: Scaling Transformers to longer sequences is limited by the quadratic memory and runtime costs of the attention layer, which currently operates at only 25-40% of a GPU's theoretical maximum speed. FlashAttention-2 addresses this by optimizing work partitioning across GPU thread blocks and warps to reduce non-matrix-multiplication operations and shared memory overhead. This method achieves a 2x speedup over the original FlashAttention, reaching up to 72% model FLOPs utilization during GPT-style model training.

title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
authors: Ji Lin, Jiaming Tang, Haotian Tang, Shang Yang, Wei-Ming Chen, Wei-Chen Wang, Guangxuan Xiao, Xingyu Dang, Chuang Gan, Song Han
reason: AWQ is a key method for weight-only quantization, a primary technique used to reduce LLM memory footprint and speed up inference.
summary: Deploying large language models on edge devices is difficult due to their massive size and limited hardware resources. The AWQ method identifies the 1% most important weight channels by analyzing activation distributions and applies an equivalent mathematical transformation to scale them, reducing quantization error without requiring complex retraining. This approach enables efficient 4-bit quantization that outperforms existing methods and allows 70B parameter models to run on mobile GPUs.

title:
TurboTransformers: An Efficient GPU Serving System For Transformer
  Models
authors: Jiarui Fang, Yang Yu, Chengduo Zhao, Jie Zhou
reason: Focuses on GPU serving optimization (batching, memory, scheduling) for Transformers, which is foundational to modern LLM inference efficiency.
summary: Serving Transformer models in data centers is difficult due to high computational demands and the memory management challenges posed by variable-length input sequences. TurboTransformers addresses this by implementing a parallelized GPU algorithm for reduction operations, a specialized memory allocation strategy, and a dynamic programming-based batch scheduler. The system achieves state-of-the-art serving performance on GPU platforms and can be integrated into existing PyTorch workflows with minimal code changes.
